home.h1_line1: One VPN for calls, messengers and AI
home.intro: 100–200 Mbps speed, up to 3 devices per account, configs always at hand in your dashboard. Card payment. Download the client, paste the key, connect.
home.funnel_desc: We give you an hour on the same server as the paid plan. Call on Telegram, open ChatGPT, check the speed — then decide. No card needed at this step.
home.funnel_note: Sign in with an emailed code, no passwords needed. Pay before the trial ends and the same key keeps working — no need to reissue it. One trial per account; the key switches off on its own after an hour, no charges.
home.payment_body: We accept Visa, Mastercard and MIR — Russian and international. RUB for Russian cards, USD or EUR for others. Payment is processed via Lava; we never store card data.
home.ip_body: We monitor server health. If your carrier or provider blocks the current address, a new key appears in your dashboard and the old one disappears — no ticket needed, no manual reconfiguration.
home.why_body: We needed a tool where everything just works: calls, AI, IDEs. We tried the available options and figured out why some configurations hold the connection and others don't — then built ours on the most stable one we found.

vpn.h1: VPN for messenger calls and AI work
vpn.intro: Voice and video calls in Telegram and WhatsApp go through without drops, ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude open on the first try, Google AI Studio sessions don't die mid-way. Speed on most servers stays in the 100–200 Mbps range.
vpn.try_title: Test it on your own workload — one hour free
vpn.try_desc: Get a key, make a call, open the AI tools, check the speed. No card needed. Works? Get PRO. Doesn't? Just leave.
vpn.why_title: Why we built our own service
vpn.why_body: We needed a tool where everything just worked — calls, AI, dev environments. We tried the available options and each one broke somewhere: voice cutting out here, AI services not opening there. We eventually figured out what makes some configurations hold the connection and others not, and built a service on the most stable one we tested.
vpn.how_title: How it works under the hood
vpn.how_body1: It runs on AmneziaWG: WireGuard with traffic obfuscation, so the connection isn't fingerprinted as a VPN by packet signature. That's why plain WireGuard gets blocked on some networks while this keeps working.
vpn.how_body2: MTU is tuned separately: at the default value, Telegram voice calls stop going through because packets don't fit the channel and get silently dropped. We set it lower and the audio stopped breaking up. Details like this are the difference between "the VPN works" and "the VPN works for calls".
vpn.feature1: Calls in Telegram, WhatsApp and other messengers without drops or lag
vpn.feature3: Access to ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude
vpn.feature4: Google AI Studio and Antigravity sessions that don't drop
vpn.feature5: Up to 3 devices per account, configs in your dashboard
vpn.ip_title: What happens if your IP gets blocked
vpn.ip_body1: Address blocks happen — that's a normal part of running any VPN, and promising otherwise would be dishonest. What we're responsible for is making sure you never have to deal with it yourself.
vpn.ip_body2: We check server availability regularly. If your carrier or provider blocks the current address, a new key appears in your dashboard and the broken one disappears. Just paste the new key into the app — no ticket needed.
